title: How databases think: tables, queries and summaries

say: How databases think: tables, queries and summaries.
This is the video for module 1 of SQL Fundamentals.
Your bank app, a ride-hailing app, an online shop: almost all keep their records in a relational database. The data sits in several tables, linked by shared ID numbers.

say: A primary key is a column that is unique for every row and never empty. In customers, Amaka is number 1.

panel.heading: Keys and storing each fact once

cards.d: Unique for every row, never empty. Amaka is customer_id 1, and no one else can be 1.
Points to another table. Order 101 has customer_id 1, so it belongs to Amaka.
Store each fact once. Amaka's city lives only in customers, so reports never disagree.

say: A foreign key holds the primary key of another table. Order 101 has customer_id 1, so it belongs to Amaka. That one number lets you join tables later.

panel.heading: Keys and storing each fact once

cards.d: Unique for every row, never empty. Amaka is customer_id 1, and no one else can be 1.
Points to another table. Order 101 has customer_id 1, so it belongs to Amaka.
Store each fact once. Amaka's city lives only in customers, so reports never disagree.

say: Why not one big sheet? If Amaka's city is typed on every order and she moves, you must change every row, and if you miss one, your reports disagree. Storing each fact once is called normalisation.

say: Integer holds whole numbers, like IDs and quantities.

panel.heading: Choose each column's type on purpose
items: INTEGER: whole numbers, IDs, quantities
DECIMAL: exact numbers for money
TEXT: names, and phone numbers too
DATE: always YYYY-MM-DD
BOOLEAN: true or false

say: Decimal, or numeric, holds exact numbers. Use it for money, never a floating type, which can make tiny rounding errors.

say: Text holds words. Phone numbers are text too, because a leading zero, as in 0803, would be lost if stored as a number.

say: A query is a polite, precise request. SELECT names the columns you want. FROM names the table.

panel.heading: Five keywords answer most questions
items: SELECT: the columns you want
FROM: the table
WHERE: keep rows that match
ORDER BY: sort, DESC for largest first
LIMIT: keep only the first few rows

say: WHERE keeps only the rows where a condition is true. Text goes inside single quotes, numbers do not. When you mix AND with OR, use brackets, because AND is worked out first.

say: One trap. A missing value is NULL, which means unknown, and it is never equal to anything. So WHERE phone = NULL returns nothing. Always write IS NULL.

say: Kemi writes: SELECT order ID, order date and amount, FROM orders, WHERE channel is WhatsApp AND status is delivered, ORDER BY amount, descending.

say: Managers want answers, not lists. COUNT, SUM and AVG turn many rows into one number. GROUP BY gives one number per group.

card.title: Delivered sales by channel
card.note: Practice figures, not real market prices.

say: Kemi's delivered sales by channel: WhatsApp 101,000 naira, Instagram 83,000, and the website 27,500.

card.title: Delivered sales by channel
card.note: Practice figures, not real market prices.

say: Now reconcile. The groups must add back to the total. 101,000 plus 83,000 plus 27,500 is 211,500, and 4 plus 3 plus 1 is 8 orders. If the pieces do not add up, something is wrong.
And remember: every column in SELECT must be inside a function or listed in GROUP BY.

say: WHERE filters single rows before grouping, such as keeping only delivered orders.

panel.heading: WHERE or HAVING?

say: HAVING filters whole groups after the totals are made. HAVING COUNT of orders of at least 2 finds Kemi's repeat buyers: customer 1 with 3 orders, and customer 2 with 2.

panel.heading: WHERE or HAVING?

say: To remember. Tables are linked by keys, and each fact is stored once. Five keywords answer most questions. Test missing values with IS NULL. And always check that your groups add back to the total.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Tables linked by primary and foreign keys
Store each fact once
SELECT, FROM, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT
IS NULL, never = NULL
Group totals must add back to the whole
